# Haplotype statistics

You've done a lot of exercises and a lot of coding to dig into various summary
statistics you can explore with _slendr_, all of whom were based, one way or
another, on allele frequencies and allele frequency correlations.

There's one last class of modeling tools which are important for you to learn,
and those are methods based on haplotypes---i.e., continuous segments of DNA
inherited from generation to generation, continuously broken up by
recombination.

To ease things off a little bit, this chapter is organized not around
thinking-intensive exercises, but more as bits of recipes demonstrating useful
_slendr_ functions based operating with haplotypes. The primary goal is to close
off our sessions on learning modeling with a few more tools before we dig into
developing modeling workflows for your own projects.
